title: Bulk Drug Park in Odisha
body_text:
The scheme for promotion of Bulk Drug Parks was approved by the Cabinet on 20.03.2020 to facilitate setting up of three (3) Bulk Drug Parks in the country with the objective to bring down the cost of manufacturing of bulk drugs by creation of world class common infrastructure facilities. It would also help in creation of economies of scale for production of bulk drugs.
Under the scheme for Promotion of Bulk Drug Parks, the Department had received proposals from thirteen states. After evaluation, proposals of Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh were approved.
There is no proposal to establish a Bulk Drug Park in Odisha under scheme for “Promotion of Bulk Drug Parks” and Production Linked Incentive scheme (PLI) or any other Central Scheme of the Department of Pharmaceuticals.
This information was given by Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Smt. Anupriya Patel, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

ministry.name: Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers :Department of Pharmaceuticals

enrichment.summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Chemicals and Fertilizers, Anupriya Patel, clarified that no Bulk Drug Park has been proposed or approved for Odisha under the Centre's scheme for Promotion of Bulk Drug Parks or under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme. Under the Bulk Drug Parks scheme, approved by the Cabinet on 20 March 2020 to set up three parks nationally, proposals were received from thirteen states but only those from Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh were approved.
enrichment.context: Bulk drugs, also called Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs), are the key raw materials used to manufacture finished pharmaceutical formulations. India has historically been heavily import-dependent on China for many critical APIs, a vulnerability starkly exposed during the COVID-19 pandemic when supply chains were disrupted. To address this strategic and economic risk, the government launched two flagship schemes in 2020: the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for bulk drugs, which incentivizes domestic manufacturing of 41 critical APIs and key starting materials, and the Scheme for Promotion of Bulk Drug Parks, which funds common infrastructure (like effluent treatment plants, power, and testing labs) to lower production costs and create economies of scale by clustering manufacturers together. These initiatives fall under the broader Atmanirbhar Bharat (self-reliant India) push for pharmaceutical and API self-sufficiency, given India's status as the 'pharmacy of the world' for generic medicines. The clarification on Odisha is a routine parliamentary response but is useful for tracking the geographic spread and implementation status of these strategic schemes, which remain limited to only three states years after their launch, indicating slow progress in reducing import dependence on APIs.
